title: Tilt
narrative: Reveal height without traveling. A body from shoes to face, a building from door to roof, a dinosaur from ankle to skull: the facts are stacked on one vertical.
The feet do not move. A crane or a jib is the wrong tool only if you wanted parallax of a rising support.
If the foreground must slide as you climb, boom. If you only need to look up, tilt.
how: Tripod, fluid head, horizontal axis. Start and end on composed frames; do not overshoot into ceiling unless that is the gag.
A wide lens exaggerates vertical stretch; a longer lens keeps the stack calmer. Prompt: Tilt on [Subject], camera rotating on its horizontal axis, climbing or descending the world from a fixed point.
when: Use it to reveal height from one stance: a statue, a tower, a person from ground to face. Do not tilt as a fake crane-up.
vs: Tilt Up and Tilt Down name direction. A Crane Up physically lifts the camera, so rooftops and streets change in parallax.
A Pedestal Up raises the support on a column without pitching. A Pan is the horizontal cousin.
examples_film: Jurassic Park tilts up bodies and gates to stack scale from a planted stance. Citizen Kane uses vertical swings and stacked compositions to turn height into power.
Grammar: rotation, not travel.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a crane-up. The tell: foreground sliding, the support rising, the person shrinking in a map.
The fix: lock the position, pitch only, and let height arrive as angle.

faq.q: What is Tilt in film?
faq.a: A tilt rotates the camera vertically from a fixed position. The tripod stays put; the frame climbs or drops to reveal height.

faq.q: Tilt vs Crane Up
faq.a: A tilt only changes angle. A crane physically moves the camera through space, so parallax appears and the map can change.

faq.q: When should I use Tilt?
faq.a: Use it to reveal height without traveling. Do not use it when you need the camera to climb and ease back over a city.

faq.q: How do I prompt Tilt for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write a planted tripod and a vertical rotation. Example: Tilt on [Subject], camera rotating on its horizontal axis, climbing or descending the world from a fixed point.

title: Tilt Down
narrative: The new fact is below: a body, a key, a grave, a child. Establishing scale above, then landing, keeps rank in the pitch of the head rather than in a descending crane.
It is the wrong tool when you must arrive from a map into a street with true height change. A tilt cannot lower the lens into a crowd; it can only look down at one.
how: Compose the high start and the low end. Control exposure as you leave the sky.
Keep the support still so the move stays pitch, not boom. Prompt a slow tilt down onto the subject, starting in sky or ceiling and descending to the figure, a measured vertical scan.
when: Use it to land on a person or object after establishing scale above. Concrete beat: a ceiling fan, then the sleeper.
Do not use it when the camera itself must come down to eye height.
vs: A Tilt Up is the opposite pitch. A Crane Down translates through height and can keep walking after the descent.
A Pedestal Down lowers the whole camera with tilt unchanged. Tilt down looks down; it does not sit down.
examples_film: Citizen Kane uses vertical looking so ceilings and power share a sentence. The Godfather lands from rooms onto faces and objects as rank.
These are pitch grammar, distinct from crane descents that change station.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Crane Down . The tell is the camera's eyeline dropping through floors, with parallax as objects rise in frame.
The fix: keep the sticks planted, pitch down, end on the lower fact.

faq.q: What is Tilt Down in film?
faq.a: It is a downward pitch of a camera that stays in one position, scanning from a higher composition to a lower one.

faq.q: Tilt Down vs Crane Down
faq.a: Crane down physically lowers (and often advances) the camera. Tilt down only rotates, so height of the lens stays put while the look drops.

faq.q: When should I use Tilt Down?
faq.a: When the story fact is below the current look and you do not need a new station. Do not use it to enter a street from the sky.

faq.q: How do I prompt Tilt Down for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write fixed camera, tilt down from sky or ceiling onto [Subject], no crane, no pedestal. Name the landing object.

title: Tilt Up
narrative: Height, awe, or a face can be delayed until the last part of the image is shown. Ground evidence connects to its source.
Scale becomes a relationship because we are forced to look up from where we already stand. It is the wrong tool when the camera must actually climb: a tilt cannot gain a rooftop's true station.
If architecture must slide down the frame with parallax, you wanted a pedestal or a crane.
how: Set a stable pivot and compose the lower and upper frames. Manage exposure if the move includes a bright sky.
Distinguish a tilt from physically lifting the camera. Prompt a slow tilt up, rotation on the horizontal axis, from ground detail to face or from face to towering architecture.
when: Use it to reveal height, awe, or a face last. Concrete beat: boots, then the rifle, then the face.
Do not use it as a fake crane that never leaves the sticks.
vs: A Crane Up and a Pedestal Up translate the camera through height, so parallax appears. A Tilt Down is the same pitch axis the other way.
A Low Angle may be a still end frame; tilt up is the motion that can arrive there.
examples_film: Psycho associates the motel with the house above it through vertical looking. Besieged connects a house's levels with vertical camera rotation.
Jurassic Park uses upward tilts so scale arrives as recognition. Confirm whether a given dinosaur reveal also dollies; the tilt is the pitch, not the track.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Crane Up or Pedestal Up . The tell is a changing eyeline height and sliding parallax of near objects.
The fix: freeze the tripod height, pitch up only, and let the top of the frame be the new fact.

faq.q: What is Tilt Up in film?
faq.a: It is a vertical rotation of a locked-off camera that pitches the lens upward, revealing higher parts of the same scene without lifting the support.

faq.q: Tilt Up vs Crane Up
faq.a: Crane up moves the camera through space, often backing away as it rises. Tilt up only turns on the head, so you look up from the same spot.

faq.q: When should I use Tilt Up?
faq.a: When height or a delayed face is the information and you are willing to stay at one station. Do not use it to fake a lift onto a roof.

faq.q: How do I prompt Tilt Up for AI image or video?
faq.a: Say fixed position, tilt up, horizontal-axis rotation, no crane, no pedestal. Name the start (ground, hem, desk) and the end (face, tower, sky).

title: Tracking Shot
narrative: Accompany a walker. The picture is not a postcard of a person; it is duration spent in their path.

Side-on tracking keeps cause, distance, and fatigue visible, which is why corridor fights and long walks live here. It is the wrong tool for a seated confession, and the wrong tool if you only panned from a locked tripod with a long lens.
If foreground does not slide, you did not track.
how: Use dolly, Steadicam, gimbal, or vehicle on a path parallel to the action. Match speed.
Hold a consistent distance and shoulder height unless the story changes rank. One direction.
Prompt a lateral tracking shot, camera matching pace on a parallel path, shoulder height, parallax of three planes.
when: Use it to accompany a walker through space that must stay readable. Concrete beat: a side-on corridor fight in which exhaustion is as visible as the hits.
Do not track a still interrogation.
vs: A Follow Shot trails behind, using the back of the head as foreground. A Walk and Talk is tracking put to conversation coverage.
Steadicam is a support that often executes tracks. A Dolly Left can track a still line; tracking as a job is subject-locked travel.
Do not confuse it with a static telephoto pan.
examples_film: Touch of Evil opens with a long traveling sentence. Children of Men and 1917 keep geography continuous while people move.
Oldboy 's hammer fight is predominantly side-on tracking in a narrow corridor. The 400 Blows ends on Antoine's run toward the sea.
Grammar of matched pace, not a stunt to copy.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Pan Left from a locked head, or a Slow Zoom In that only changes size. The tell is no sliding foreground.
The fix: a traveling support, matching pace, near objects passing.

faq.q: What is Tracking Shot in film?
faq.a: It is a camera move that travels with a subject, usually matching their pace and holding distance so the world slides past in parallax.

faq.q: Tracking Shot vs Follow Shot
faq.a: Follow typically sits behind and uses the back of the head as a foreground. Tracking is the broader job and often rides beside, keeping a side-on view of action.

faq.q: When should I use Tracking Shot?
faq.a: When walking, running, or fighting must stay continuous in space. Do not use it for a seated scene that only needed a slow push.

faq.q: How do I prompt Tracking Shot for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write camera tracks alongside [Subject] at matching pace, consistent distance, shoulder height, foreground parallax. One direction. No tripod pan.

title: Trucking
narrative: Stay beside a walker. Talk, walk, and the city or the hallway becomes a moving set.
The camera is a polite companion, not a hunter in front and not a conveyor belt. If you lead from the front, you are tracking or following.
If the world is a factory that does not care, you are on a conveyor. Trucking is the side-on companion.
how: Track parallel to the walk, camera at eye or chest, often 35 to 50mm. Match speed to the stride.
Foreground (posts, extras, doorways) should shear; the far wall crawls. Prompt: Trucking with [Subject], lateral dolly, the camera sliding sideways, a sidewalk or corridor peeling by.
when: Use it to stay beside a walker through a street or hall. Do not truck on a static portrait; then you only have a slider fidget.
vs: Dolly Left names a lateral direction on wheels. Tracking Shot is the broader follow along a path, including front and behind.
Conveyor is constant industrial speed with the person as cargo. A Pan from sticks will lose the walker or smear them.
examples_film: The Goodfellas Copacabana take includes lateral travel through service spaces as a companion. Touch of Evil moves with people through a town so the street peels.
Grammar: beside, matching speed, lateral parallax.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a pan with a walking person. The tell: the subject changes size and the background only swings.
The fix: translate sideways, match stride, keep size, let the sidewalk peel.

faq.q: What is Trucking in film?
faq.a: Trucking is a lateral dolly beside a walker. The camera slides sideways so the sidewalk or corridor peels by and the subject stays a constant size.

faq.q: Trucking vs Tracking
faq.a: Tracking is the general follow along a path, including front and behind. Trucking is specifically the side-on, lateral companion.

faq.q: When should I use Trucking?
faq.a: Use it to stay beside a person walking and talking. Do not use it on a locked portrait.

faq.q: How do I prompt Trucking for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write a lateral dolly matching walk speed. Example: Trucking with [Subject], lateral dolly, the camera sliding sideways, a sidewalk or corridor peeling by.

title: Walk and Talk
narrative: Talk does not pause for a room, and the room does not pause for talk. Doorways, extras, and turning corners become the punctuation of the lines.
The job is coverage of conversation in motion, not a silent hunt. It is the wrong tool for a chase with no words, and the wrong tool for a seated interrogation.
If nobody is walking while talking, it is just a track.
how: Steadicam or gimbal, often leading, sometimes flanking. Hold a moving medium, shoulder height, leave headroom for doorways.
Recorders and extras must be blocked as part of the path. Prompt walk-and-talk tracking, camera leading or flanking at medium, architecture flowing, corridor energy.
when: Use it when information and geography must move together. Concrete beat: two people argue policy while threading a bullpen, never sitting.
Do not walk-and-talk a scene that wants a table.
vs: Tracking Shot is the broader travel job and may be silent action. A Follow Shot hides faces behind heads.
Steadicam is the usual support. Walk-and-talk is specifically dialogue plus path: West Wing grammar, not a hammer fight.
examples_film: The West Wing made corridor walk-and-talk the series' coverage engine. The Social Network uses walking conversation so status and architecture share the lines.
Birdman is a cousin in longer connecting talk. Speech in motion: that is the grammar.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a silent Follow Shot or a seated two-shot with a slow Dolly In . The tell is the back of a head, or feet that do not walk.
The fix: people talking while walking, camera leading or flanking, faces readable, rooms changing.

faq.q: What is Walk and Talk in film?
faq.a: It is moving coverage of conversation: the camera travels with people who are walking while they speak, so the lines and the building unfold together.

faq.q: Walk and Talk vs Tracking Shot
faq.a: Tracking can follow a silent walker or a fight. Walk-and-talk requires dialogue in motion, usually as a leading or flanking medium.

faq.q: When should I use Walk and Talk?
faq.a: When exposition or argument should happen on the move through a workplace or campus. Do not use it for a still confession.

faq.q: How do I prompt Walk and Talk for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write camera leads or flanks [Subject] walking and talking, moving medium, architecture flowing, faces readable. Ban a silent follow from behind.

title: Wandering
narrative: Looking is the action. Openings, parties, streets: the lens behaves like a guest who has not decided what matters.
Discovery is the point, not a pre-aimed hero. Once the camera knows the target and drives at it, the wandering is over.
A hunt is a track. A tour that never finds anything is also empty: curiosity still needs a world worth searching.
how: Steadicam or handheld, human height, no locked axis. Speed is uneven on purpose.
Let the frame glance off extras, corners, and unfinished business, then arrive. Prompt: Wandering camera near [Subject], unmotivated drift that becomes curiosity, a search without a target yet.
when: Use it when the scene is a search: an opening that discovers a location, a camera that has not chosen a side. Do not wander through a scene whose power geography is already known.
vs: Handheld is a body and a shake; it can still be aimed. Steadicam is a float that can wander or can be a laser.
Wandering is the motive: discovery, not targeting. A Pan from sticks surveys from one point; wandering translates.
examples_film: Children of Men openings let the camera discover a street before the event lands. The Player 's start wanders a lot as a search that becomes a sentence.
Grammar: looking before knowing.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a hero-cam walk or a clean track. The tell: the subject is already centered and inevitable.
The fix: drift, miss, then find; let the space exist before the aim.

faq.q: What is Wandering in film?
faq.a: A wandering camera searches a space without a chosen target yet. Looking is the action; discovery comes after the drift.

faq.q: Wandering vs Handheld
faq.a: Handheld is a mounting and a shake. Wandering is a motive: curiosity rather than a pre-aimed subject. A wander can be smooth on a vest.

faq.q: When should I use Wandering?
faq.a: Use it for openings and searches, when the camera has not chosen a side. Do not wander a scene whose blocking is already the point.

faq.q: How do I prompt Wandering for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write a drift that discovers rather than targets. Example: Wandering camera near [Subject], unmotivated drift that becomes curiosity, a search without a target yet.

title: Whip Pan
narrative: The move is a transition, a punchline, or a sudden shift of attention. Energy transfers between spaces that may not even be adjacent.
An ordinary change of location can feel like a comic snap if the blur matches. It is the wrong tool for a readable pan across a mural, and the wrong tool if you need to see the travel.
If the landing is not sharp, the whip is only a smear.
how: Match blur direction, luminance, duration, and acceleration if you cut inside the blur. Design the sharp landing before generating the two sides.
Opposite pan directions or mismatched brightness expose the seam. Prompt a violent whip pan off the subject, horizontal motion blur streaking the world, then a snap resolve on the next beat.
when: Use it as a transition, punchline, or sudden attention shift. Concrete beat: a look off, a blur, a new room already in progress.
Do not whip across information the audience must read.
vs: A Pan Left or Pan Right stays readable. A Whip Tilt is the same idea on the pitch axis.
A Crash Zoom In blurs radially by changing focal length, not by yaw. Whip pan is horizontal speed past recognition, then a hard stop.
examples_film: Shaun of the Dead compresses routine and travel with fast visual joins. Hot Fuzz accelerates exposition with whip-like moves.
Baby Driver and Whiplash time the blur to music and hits. Use the matched smear and the landing, not the playlist.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a fast Pan Right that never blurs, or a Crash Zoom In . The tell is readable detail in the middle, radial zoom blur, or a seam where blur directions disagree.
The fix: commit to unreadability in the middle, match the join, stop sharp.

faq.q: What is Whip Pan in film?
faq.a: It is a pan so fast that the frame becomes horizontal motion blur, often used to hide a cut or to sting a new composition.

faq.q: Whip Pan vs Crash Zoom In
faq.a: Crash zoom in changes focal length and blurs radially. Whip pan rotates the camera on yaw and blurs sideways, then resolves on a new aim.

faq.q: When should I use Whip Pan?
faq.a: When you need a snap of attention or an invisible join between two setups. Do not use it to show a landscape.

faq.q: How do I prompt Whip Pan for AI image or video?
faq.a: Demand extremely fast horizontal pan, heavy motion blur, then a sharp stop on a named landing. If used as a cut, match blur direction on both sides.

title: Whip Tilt
narrative: Vertical shock instead of a horizontal whip. A body hits the floor, a face is found in a tree, a sign slams down from sky.
The middle of the move should be unreadable on purpose. It is the wrong tool for a slow reveal of a tower, and the wrong tool if you needed the camera to fall with a body.
Blurred pitch is not a crane collapse.
how: Rotate on the horizontal axis past blur, then hard-stop on a composed frame. Match blur if you cut inside it.
Keep the tripod planted so you do not add a drop. Prompt a violent vertical whip tilt, the frame ripping up or down with motion blur, then a hard stop.
when: Use it for vertical shock instead of a horizontal whip. Concrete beat: from a screaming mouth down onto the weapon that caused it.
Do not use it to measure a building.
vs: A Whip Pan blurs on yaw. A Tilt Up or Tilt Down stays readable on the same axis.
A Crash Zoom In is optical, not a head rotation. Whip tilt is pitch speed, then a stop.
examples_film: Evil Dead throws the camera through violent vertical reorientations as shock grammar. Crank uses similar speed as body panic.
These are references for blur-and-stop, not for copying specific gags.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Whip Pan or a fast Tilt Down that remains readable. The tell is horizontal streaks, or a clear building in the middle of the move.
The fix: vertical blur, planted support, sharp landing.

faq.q: What is Whip Tilt in film?
faq.a: It is a tilt so fast that the image streaks vertically, then a hard stop on a new high or low composition.

faq.q: Whip Tilt vs Whip Pan
faq.a: Whip pan blurs horizontally by yawing. Whip tilt blurs vertically by pitching. Both plant the support and hide the middle in speed.

faq.q: When should I use Whip Tilt?
faq.a: When the shock is above or below, not beside. Do not use it for a gentle height reveal.

faq.q: How do I prompt Whip Tilt for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write extremely fast vertical tilt, heavy motion blur, hard stop on a named end frame. Specify up or down. No crane travel.

title: Wiggle
narrative: Add life to a lock-off without a real move. Lenticular photos, stereo gifs, a still that breathes: depth as a fidget.
Near objects shift a little; the far wall almost holds. If the camera walks, you have parallax as a path, not a wiggle.
A full slider is already too much. The point is two nearby viewpoints, not a tour.
how: Nodal shift of a few centimeters, or a pair of stills played as a loop. Subject mostly still.
Prompt: Wiggle cam on [Subject], tiny stereo rock, a living postcard, depth as a fidget.
when: Use it to wake a still without committing to a move. Do not use it as coverage of a walk.
vs: Wigglegram is the lenticular or stereo-gif cousin, often a pair of stills. Parallax is the optical fact; a wiggle is parallax as a tiny rock.
A Slider Shot travels 60 to 120 centimeters, which is already a real move.
examples_film: Lenticular photos and TikTok stereo are the grammar: two nearby eyes, a postcard that lives. Not a narrative dolly.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a slider or a dolly. The tell: the background really travels, the path is a meter.
The fix: rock between two nearby viewpoints, stereo fidget only.

faq.q: What is Wiggle in film?
faq.a: A wiggle is a tiny stereo rock between two nearby viewpoints, centimeters of travel, so a lock-off reads as a living postcard.

faq.q: Wiggle vs Parallax
faq.a: Parallax is the relative motion of planes when the camera translates any distance. Wiggle is that fact used as a fidget, not as a path.

faq.q: When should I use Wiggle?
faq.a: Use it to add life to a still without a real move. Do not use it to cover a walk.

faq.q: How do I prompt Wiggle for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write a tiny stereo rock between two nearby viewpoints. Example: Wiggle cam on [Subject], tiny stereo rock, a living postcard, depth as a fidget.

title: YoYo Zoom
narrative: One axis, two punches. A thought that arrives and leaves, a sting, a joke: crash in, crash out, same breath.
Hold at neither end for long. A funeral may not want it.
A slow zoom that wanders is not a yoyo. Crash zoom in is a one-way punch; this is a punch and a release.
how: Locked body, zoom lens. In then out (or out then in) on one axis, short duration.
Comic or violent depending on speed. Prompt: Yo-yo zoom on [Subject], in and out on the same axis, a punch then a release, optical breathing.
when: Use it for a sting or a joke on one optical axis. Do not use a slow hunt and call it a yoyo.
vs: Crash Zoom In is one way in. Crash Zoom Out is one way out.
Zoom is the parent optical change. Yoyo does both in one breath.
A Rapid Zoom In snaps in and holds.
examples_film: Shaun of the Dead uses snap zooms as comic grammar, including in-and-out breaths. Music videos treat optical breathing as percussion.
Grammar: punch then release, body still.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a slow zoom or a one-way crash. The tell: it never comes back, or it crawls.
The fix: snap both ways on a locked body, no wheels.

faq.q: What is YoYo Zoom in film?
faq.a: A yoyo zoom is an in-then-out (or out-then-in) on the optical axis in one breath, camera body still. A punch and a release.

faq.q: YoYo Zoom vs Crash Zoom In
faq.a: A crash zoom in is a one-way punch that holds. A yoyo zoom returns on the same axis in the same breath.

faq.q: When should I use YoYo Zoom?
faq.a: Use it for a sting, a joke, or a thought that arrives and leaves. Do not use it as a slow search.

faq.q: How do I prompt YoYo Zoom for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write in then out on one axis, body still. Example: Yo-yo zoom on [Subject], in and out on the same axis, a punch then a release, optical breathing.

title: Zoom
narrative: Change size without walking. Surveillance, emphasis, a punch: the glass does the work.
The background does not shear; it merely occupies more or less of the frame. If you need the room to be real, dolly.
The compound cousin is a dolly zoom, where travel and glass disagree on purpose. A zoom used as fake geography will flatten the set and give the cheat away.
how: Locked body, zoom lens, often on sticks. In flattens (more telephoto); out opens (more wide).
No near-object shear. Prompt: Zoom on [Subject], optical magnification, camera body still, space flattening or opening without parallax.
when: Use it to change size from one stance: a watcher's glass, a snap to a face, a slow tightening. Do not label a dolly as a zoom.
vs: Slow Zoom In is the same axis at a crawl. Crash Zoom In is the punch.
A Dolly Zoom pairs opposite travel and glass so perspective warps. A Dolly translates and produces parallax.
examples_film: The Conversation uses optical magnification as surveillance, glass doing the watching. Jaws is famous for a dolly zoom, the other move: do not cite that beach shock as a plain zoom.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a dolly-in. The tell: a lamp shears, a doorway slides, true parallax.
The fix: lock the camera, change only focal length, and let planes scale together.

faq.q: What is Zoom in film?
faq.a: A zoom changes focal length while the camera body stays put. Size changes; parallax does not appear.

faq.q: Zoom vs Dolly
faq.a: A dolly moves the camera through space, so near objects shear. A zoom only changes the lens, so the world scales as one card.

faq.q: When should I use Zoom?
faq.a: Use it to change size without walking: surveillance, a snap, a slow tighten. Do not use it to fake a walk through a room.

faq.q: How do I prompt Zoom for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write optical magnification and no camera travel. Example: Zoom on [Subject], optical magnification, camera body still, space flattening or opening without parallax.

title: Bleach Bypass
narrative: The world looks abrasive, contaminated, or exhausted. Combat, crime, and unforgiving cities live here because color has been punished, not tastefully split.
Skin can go towards brass or grey. Blacks pack down.
It is a coordinated tonal system, not just the removal of hue. It is the wrong tool when you wanted complementary studio punch.

Teal and Orange keeps faces warm and skies cyan; bleach-bypass does not throw a party on the color wheel. It is also the wrong tool if you need full Monochrome : there is still some chroma, just crushed.
A simple Desaturation without the silver contrast is a paler, softer cousin.
how: For a digital recreation, grade contrast, saturation, and highlight roll-off separately and test skin. Lift nothing in the blacks that should stay packed.
Keep a little hue so it does not collapse into black and white unless that is the intent. Original films may use different negative, intermediate, or print treatments; do not assume one lab recipe.
Prompt: Bleach-bypass look on [Subject], retained silver, crushed color, harsh contrast, metallic midtones.
when: Use it for war, crime, or a world without mercy: a landing, a hunt through rain, a fluorescent interrogation. Do not use it as a synonym for teal-orange action gloss, and do not call every desaturated image bleach-bypass.
vs: Desaturation only pulls chroma; contrast and silver behavior may stay gentle. Monochrome removes hue entirely.
Teal and Orange is a complementary grade with warm skin. Tonal Contrast is how you place dark against light in the rectangle, not a lab process.
examples_film: Saving Private Ryan 's combat imagery has a harsh, desaturated, high-contrast character associated with silver retention. Se7en packs interiors and city scenes with dense shadows and restrained color.
Minority Report is often cited for a related cold, dense, drained finish. Grammar of density, not a still to clone.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Teal and Orange or mild Desaturation . The tell is warm peach skin against cyan night, or a flat grey wash with no extra density.
Fix: packed blacks, harsh highlights, drained but not absent color, metallic mids. A look label does not verify the exact photochemical stage of a particular release.

faq.q: What is bleach bypass in film?
faq.a: It is a silver-retention process, or a digital imitation, that leaves metallic density in the image. Contrast and grain go up, saturation goes down, and highlights look harsh.

faq.q: Bleach Bypass vs Desaturation
faq.a: Desaturation only reduces chroma. Bleach bypass also densifies the image: deeper blacks, harsher highlights, a metallic leftover. Drained color without that density is not bleach-bypass.

faq.q: When should I use bleach bypass?
faq.a: Use it for war, crime, or any world that should feel merciless and abrasive. Skip it for studio complementary gloss and for true black and white.

faq.q: How do I prompt bleach bypass for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Bleach-bypass look on [Subject], retained silver, crushed color, harsh contrast, metallic midtones. Forbid teal-orange skin splits and candy saturation.

title: Color Shift
narrative: Dorothy opens a door and the world gains hue. A zone, a lie, a memory: the threshold can be a cut, a doorway, or a grade that travels inside the take.
The audience crosses with the character. A global saturation ramp is different from a color world revealed through a door.
It is the wrong tool when the film simply has more than one static Palette across chapters. Palettes can sit still; a shift is a change you watch.
It is also the wrong tool for Cross Process or Split Toning that never move. If the beat is one loud world from the first frame, you wanted Hyper-Saturation or a locked palette, not a shift.
how: Choose whether the change occurs across a cut, through an opening, or gradually inside the image. Match production design and exposure so the arrival of color (or of a new temperature) feels intended.

If you go from grey to hue, expose the grey chapter so the later color has somewhere to live. Prompt: Color shift across [Subject], hues sliding mid-shot or mid-grade, a world that changes temperature in front of us.
For video: The grade around [Subject] shifts hue during the shot, warmth turning cold or the reverse.
when: Use it when color is the event: a door onto a new world, a lie that changes temperature, a zone. Do not use it as a random hue drift, and do not call two static chapter palettes a shift unless we watch the change.
vs: Palette assigns stable hue systems to strands or places. Split Toning is a static two-hue curve.
Cross Process is a skewed primary look. Monochrome is a state you might leave.
Color-shift is the transition.
examples_film: The Wizard of Oz makes the farmhouse door a threshold into hue. Stalker changes visual treatment between the outside world and the Zone.
Hero retells events in different dominant colors; some transitions are chapter cuts, which is palette as much as shift. Suspiria (2018) lets color states mutate with the story.
Grammar of a threshold, not a still of a ruby shoe.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a static Palette or a Split Toning that never moves. The tell is two looks in two scenes with no threshold, or a random hue drift.
Fix: a defined before-state, a defined after-state, and a visible crossing (door, cut, or traveling grade).

faq.q: What is a color shift in film?
faq.a: It is a noticeable change of color state: grey to hue, warm to cold, or one world-color to another. The change is the event, whether across a door, a cut, or a traveling grade.

faq.q: Color Shift vs Split Toning
faq.a: Split toning is a stable pair of highlight and shadow hues. A color shift is a transition the audience watches. If the pair never moves, it is not a shift.

faq.q: When should I use a color shift?
faq.a: Use it when crossing a world, a lie, or a memory should be visible as color. Skip it when each chapter simply has its own still palette.

faq.q: How do I prompt a color shift for AI image or video?
faq.a: Name the before and after and the threshold. For video: the grade around [Subject] shifts hue during the shot, warmth turning cold or the reverse. For a still, show the crossing (a door, a wipe of hue). Forbid a static LUT.

title: Cool Blue
narrative: Cold institutions, night, or alienation live in this family. A hospital, a CIA office, a pre-dawn street: the air has no honey.
Skin goes toward porcelain or grey-pink. One tungsten desk lamp, if you allow it, becomes the only hearth.
It is the wrong tool when you are faking night with underexposed sun. That is Day for Night , a capture trick, not only a blue LUT.

It is the wrong tool for sculpted moon as a key on a dark set: Moonlight Gel is a lighting decision. It is also the wrong tool if the complementary split of Teal and Orange is what you actually wanted (warm skin, teal air, not an overall steel wash).
how: Bias white balance or the grade toward high Kelvin in the mids and shadows. Hold or isolate a warm practical if the scene needs one hearth.
Keep skin just readable; full cyan faces look sick unless that is the line. Night windows and fluorescent rooms already help.
Prompt: Cool blue grade on [Subject], steel shadows, hospital or moonlight, warmth reserved for one practical if any.
when: Use it for cold institutions, night, or alienation: a lawyer in a glass tower at 5 a.m., a clinic corridor. Do not use it as a synonym for day-for-night, and do not steel every romance interior.
vs: Blue Hour is actual dusk light, a capture window. Day for Night turns daylight into a night reading.
Moonlight Gel is a cool key on set. Warm Amber is the opposing overall grade.
Teal and Orange keeps skin warm on purpose.
examples_film: The Bourne Ultimatum runs steel-green-blue through offices, streets, and stations so the institution never thaws. Michael Clayton uses cold corporate and night hues against the few warmer domestic scraps.
Grammar of withheld warmth, not a copied still.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Teal and Orange (skin stays warm) or Day for Night (hard shadows from a high sun). The tell is peach faces against cyan, or daytime sky structure.
Fix: overall cool bias, maybe one warm practical, no high-sun day cues.

faq.q: What is cool blue in film?
faq.a: It is an overall cool color grade: steel, cyan, or moonlight blues in shadows and mids. Warmth is scarce and usually limited to a chosen practical.

faq.q: Cool Blue vs Teal and Orange
faq.a: Teal-orange protects warm skin and splits the rest toward cyan. Cool blue chills the whole world, faces included unless you reserve one lamp. One is a complementary split. The other is a cold wash.

faq.q: When should I use cool blue?
faq.a: Use it for institutions, night, or alienation. Skip it when you needed complementary punch, sculpted moon lighting, or a day-for-night capture.

faq.q: How do I prompt cool blue for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Cool blue grade on [Subject], steel shadows, hospital or moonlight, warmth reserved for one practical if any. Forbid peach-and-teal complementary splits and obvious daytime sun.

title: Cross Process
narrative: Wrong chemistry on purpose. Fashion films and music videos of the 1990s used the accident as style: skies go odd, shadows pick up cyan or green, skin slides toward magenta or jaundice.
The world looks like a lab error you kept. It is the wrong tool when you wanted true hues only louder.
That is Hyper-Saturation . It is the wrong tool for a designed complementary split with protected skin ( Teal and Orange ).
Vaporwave may borrow skewed primaries as a genre costume; cross-process is the chemical alibi, not the nostalgia package.
how: Offset primary relationships: push shadows toward cyan or green, let highlights go yellow, magenta, or red depending on the stock story, and raise contrast. Skin will not grade like a commercial unless you isolate it, which fights the look.
Do not randomly assign hues shot to shot; pick one accident and keep it. Prompt: Cross-processed look on [Subject], skewed primaries, cyan shadows, magenta skin shift, music-video chemical accident.
when: Use it when the image should look like a kept lab error: a 1990s fashion clip, a music video, an unreliable night. Do not use it as loud-but-true color, and do not confuse it with teal-orange.
vs: Hyper-Saturation intensifies correct hues. Teal and Orange is a controlled complementary grade.
Vaporwave is a genre palette. Color Shift is a change of color state over time or across a threshold.
Cross-process is a skewed primary relationship from the start.
examples_film: 1990s fashion films and music videos are the grammar: chemical accident as style, not a single canonical feature. When a narrative film borrows it, the tell is displaced primaries rather than simple loud red.
Treat those clips as the reference class.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Hyper-Saturation or Teal and Orange . The tell is correct reds that are only louder, or peach faces on cyan streets in a studio-split pattern.
Fix: hues that have slipped to the wrong neighbors, contrasty accident, skin not commercially protected.

faq.q: What is cross process in film?
faq.a: It is the look of film developed in the wrong chemistry, or a digital imitation of that mismatch. Primaries skew, contrast often rises, and skin and shadows take on unnatural neighbors.

faq.q: Cross Process vs Hyper-Saturation
faq.a: Hyper-saturation makes true hues louder. Cross-process puts hues in the wrong place: cyan shadows, magenta skin, yellow highlights. Loud is not the same as wrong.

faq.q: When should I use cross process?
faq.a: Use it for a kept chemical accident: fashion, music video, unreliable color. Skip it when hues should be true, even if loud, or when you wanted a teal-orange split.

faq.q: How do I prompt cross process for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Cross-processed look on [Subject], skewed primaries, cyan shadows, magenta skin shift, music-video chemical accident. Forbid correct loud primaries and protected peach skin.

title: Day for Night
narrative: You cannot wait for night, or night must still show a desert, a ranch, a ridge. The sun is skipped, flagged, or placed as a hard moon.

Underexposure and a cool bias sell darkness, but headlights, windows, and eyes must still find something to see. It is the wrong tool when you can light a real night with a sculpted moon ( Moonlight Gel ) and do not need miles of terrain.

It is the wrong tool if you only grade a day interior steel ( Cool Blue ) without hiding day cues: blue sky, short hard shadows from high sun, warm unlit windows. Ordinary day-for-night and a special high-sensitivity or infrared capture system are not the same production method.
how: Control daylight direction, often shooting when the sun is lower or back, and underexpose. Avoid obvious daytime cues (pale blue zenith, visible sun disc, lit-looking clouds).
Reshape color toward moonlight. More advanced approaches combine differently sensitive captures.
Do not equate the technique with simply making footage blue. Prompt: Day-for-night treatment of [Subject], underexposed daylight, blue wash, skipped-over sun, moonlight as a lie that reads.
when: Use it when you cannot wait for night, or night must still show terrain: a desert chase, a ranch under a false moon. Do not use it as a blue LUT on a sunny street with the sun in frame.
vs: Cool Blue is a grade, including on true night or interiors. Moonlight Gel is a cool key you hang.
Blue Hour is real twilight. Tungsten Balance can turn daylight windows blue as mixed color, which is not the same as selling a whole landscape as night.
examples_film: Classic Westerns often sold day as night to keep horses and mesas readable. Mad Max: Fury Road has stylized blue night passages in the desert.
Nope 's ranch-at-night work uses a specific capture approach that should not be flattened into ordinary day-for-night. Grammar of terrain-at-night, not a copied sky.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Cool Blue LUT on obvious day, or underexposed day that still shows a white sky and short noon shadows. The tell is blue-tinted sunlight with the sun in shot.
Fix: skip the sun, underexpose, cool the key, keep terrain, kill daytime sky cues.

faq.q: What is day for night in film?
faq.a: It is daylight photography transformed to read as night while retaining enough information to show large spaces. Exposure, sky, and highlights do the work, not only a blue tint.

faq.q: Day for Night vs Cool Blue
faq.a: Cool blue is a grade you can put on any capture. Day-for-night is a way of shooting or transforming daylight so it passes as night. If the sun and a pale zenith are still obvious, you have only tinted day.

faq.q: When should I use day for night?
faq.a: Use it when night must show terrain you cannot light, or when true night is impractical. Skip it when you can sculpt a real moon key, and skip a blue LUT on unhidden day.

faq.q: How do I prompt day for night for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Day-for-night treatment of [Subject], underexposed daylight, blue wash, skipped-over sun, moonlight as a lie that reads. Forbid a visible sun and a pale daytime sky.

title: Desaturation
narrative: Drain the world without going fully mono. A grey-green England, a dusty border, a road the color of ash: emotion sits in whatever hue remains, a red taillight or a pale face.
The audience feels the withholding. It is the wrong tool when you needed silver density and harsh highlights.
That is Bleach Bypass . It is the wrong tool when hue should be gone entirely ( Monochrome ) or when feeling should be louder than fact ( Hyper-Saturation ).
A teal-orange split can coexist with moderate saturation; do not confuse a complementary grade with a drain.
how: Pull global chroma down, then decide which accents survive (a practical, a costume, blood). Keep contrast independent: desaturation is not automatically high contrast.
Skin should stay identifiable as skin, just quieter. Prompt: Desaturated palette on [Subject], chroma pulled back, dusty, wintered, emotion in leftover color accents.
when: Use it to drain the world without going fully mono: a refugee road, a winter city, a moral hangover. Do not use it as bleach-bypass, and do not desaturate until nothing but grey remains unless you meant monochrome.
vs: Bleach Bypass adds silver contrast and metallic mids on top of a drain. Monochrome is zero chroma.
Cool Blue is a hue family, which may still be saturated. Hyper-Saturation is the opposite lever.
examples_film: Children of Men winters a near-future England so leftover color hurts. Sicario dusts the border until chroma is a ration.
The Road goes further, almost ash. Grammar of withheld hue, not a copied sky.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Bleach Bypass or Monochrome . The tell is metallic packed blacks with harsh grain, or zero hue.
Fix: quieter chroma, identifiable leftover color, contrast set independently of the drain.

faq.q: What is desaturation in film?
faq.a: It is a reduction of color intensity with hue still present. The image looks dusty or wintered, and leftover accents carry what emotion remains.

faq.q: Desaturation vs Bleach Bypass
faq.a: Desaturation is a chroma lever. Bleach bypass is silver retention: denser contrast, metallic highlights, crushed color as a system. You can desaturate gently without that density.

faq.q: When should I use desaturation?
faq.a: Use it when the world should be drained but not drawn in grey ink. Skip it for merciless silver processes and for loud, lacquered color.

faq.q: How do I prompt desaturation for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Desaturated palette on [Subject], chroma pulled back, dusty, wintered, emotion in leftover color accents. Forbid full monochrome and bleach-bypass metal.

title: Filmic Faded
narrative: The image looks like it could have gone through a projector. Shadows have air.
Bright windows go creamy instead of digital-clipped. Romance and memory often live here because the display already forgives, but the hues can still be present and modern.

It is the wrong tool when you need packed, merciless blacks ( Bleach Bypass or a hard digital contrast). It is the wrong tool if the fade is meant as expired dyes and period chemistry as a whole costume: that is Vintage .
Vintage Cine Glass is the taking lens; you can shoot modern glass and still fade the print. Film Grain is texture you may add, not the fade itself.
how: Lift the toe (blacks sit at a low grey, not 0). Roll the shoulder so highlights compress instead of hard-clipping.
Keep saturation moderate unless the story is candy. A print-emulation LUT is a starting point; still check skin and that blacks are lifted, not milky-brown by accident.
Prompt: Filmic faded grade on [Subject], lifted blacks, rolled-off highlights, print-emulation, slightly expired romance.
when: Use it when the display should feel like a print rather than HDR: a summer memory, a period-adjacent present. Do not use it on a look that needs crushed blacks, and do not treat fade as a substitute for vintage glass.
vs: Vintage is a broader past-as-chemistry treatment (dye fade, period). Vintage Cine Glass is the lens.
Film Grain is grain. Bleach Bypass packs density instead of lifting the toe.
Natural Grade can be print-like or not; natural is about hue honesty, not the toe and shoulder.
examples_film: The Master often sits in a print-like contrast with air in the blacks. Call Me by Your Name lets summer highlights roll instead of biting like video.
Grammar of toe and shoulder, not a still of a peach.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Bleach Bypass (packed, harsh) or a milky brown wash. The tell is crushed blacks, or a foggy image with no rolled shoulder.
Fix: lifted toe, compressed highlights, hues still present, contrast like a print.

faq.q: What is filmic faded in film?
faq.a: It is a print-emulation grade: lifted blacks, rolled-off highlights, contrast that sits like photochemical display rather than HDR video. Hues may still be present.

faq.q: Filmic Faded vs Vintage Cine Glass
faq.a: Vintage cine is the taking lens: coatings, swirl, optical bloom. Filmic faded is the curve of the grade: toe and shoulder of a print. You can fade a modern prime, and you can shoot old glass without lifting the blacks.

faq.q: When should I use filmic faded?
faq.a: Use it when the image should feel like a print, not like HDR. Skip it when blacks must pack down, or when you only needed grain or old glass.

faq.q: How do I prompt filmic faded for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Filmic faded grade on [Subject], lifted blacks, rolled-off highlights, print-emulation, slightly expired romance. Forbid crushed bleach-bypass blacks and HDR clip.

title: Hyper-Saturation
narrative: Reds become wet enamel. Greens look poisonous or operatic.
A dance academy, a wuxia desert, a Hong Kong corridor: the world is painted, and the paint is the emotion. Accents do not hide; they shout.
It is the wrong tool when the location's real color science should be believed. That is Natural Grade .

It is the wrong tool for a complementary studio split that still wants plausible skin ( Teal and Orange ), and it is not a chemical accident ( Cross Process ), which skews primaries off their true identities. Giallo often uses this lever, but giallo is a genre system, not the saturation knob.
how: Push chroma, especially in chosen primaries, while watching skin. You may isolate skin to protect it or let it go with the fever.
Contrast can be high or candy-flat; saturation is independent. Production design should already supply the hues you will amplify, or the grade will invent plastic color.
Prompt: Hyper-saturated color on [Subject], Velvia intensity, reds like lacquer, a dream or a fever, not documentary.
when: Use it when feeling is louder than fact: a nightmare corridor, a told-and-retold battle, a romance that is all dye. Do not use it on a documentary claim, and do not confuse it with teal-orange punch.
vs: Teal and Orange is a complementary split, often at moderate-to-high but controlled chroma. Cross Process misplaces hues (cyan shadows, magenta skin).
Giallo is a genre package that frequently includes this intensity. Desaturation is the opposite lever.
examples_film: Suspiria (1977) treats color as a physical force, reds and blues at full scream. Hero organizes versions of a story as saturated fields of cloth and desert.
In the Mood for Love lets corridor and cheongsam dyes run hotter than life. Grammar of intensity, not a still of a lamp.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Teal and Orange (controlled complementary) or Cross Process (wrong primaries). The tell is cyan shadows with peach skin, or hues that have slipped to the wrong neighbors.
Fix: true hues, louder than life, design that already holds those colors.

faq.q: What is hyper-saturation in film?
faq.a: It is color intensity pushed past ordinary record so hues look like lacquer or fever. The image is not claiming documentary fact.

faq.q: Hyper-Saturation vs Teal and Orange
faq.a: Teal-orange is a complementary pairing with protected warm skin. Hyper-saturation is a volume knob on chroma, any hues. You can have quiet teal-orange or loud red-and-green opera.

faq.q: When should I use hyper-saturation?
faq.a: Use it when emotion should outrun realism: dream, fever, operatic genre. Skip it when the location must be believed as itself.

faq.q: How do I prompt hyper-saturation for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Hyper-saturated color on [Subject], Velvia intensity, reds like lacquer, a dream or a fever, not documentary. Name the loud hues. Forbid naturalistic documentary color and teal-orange as a substitute.

title: Monochrome
narrative: Strip to drawing. A lighthouse, a boxing ring, a list of names: without hue, costume and light have to carry rank.
Skin becomes a grey. Blood becomes a density.
The audience reads edges and tones the way they read a print. It is the wrong tool when leftover color is the point.
Desaturation still lets a red coat or a yellow lamp speak. Bleach Bypass keeps a little chroma under silver.
Sepia is not black and white; it is a brown-gold world. If a single object must arrive in hue inside a grey film, that is a Color Shift or a selective hold-out, not this technique used honestly.
how: Capture in color or in a panchromatic/orthochromatic black-and-white workflow, then discard chroma or never record it. Expose for a full grey scale: hats, skies, and faces need separation that hue is no longer providing.

Orthochromatic stocks darken lips and skies differently than panchromatic; if you specify a stock era, keep that physics. Prompt: Monochrome treatment of [Subject], silver highlights, deep blacks, no chroma, shape and light only.
when: Use it when the scene should be a drawing: a confession in a tower, a fight, a historical record. Do not use it if a leftover color accent is doing the emotional work, and do not confuse it with a brown memory tone.
vs: Desaturation keeps hue at a lower intensity. Bleach Bypass drains and densifies but is not fully grey.
Sepia tints the whole scale brown-gold. Tonal Contrast is how blacks and whites are placed; monochrome is the missing chroma.
examples_film: The Lighthouse commits to a hard black-and-white world of texture and rank. Raging Bull uses monochrome so boxing becomes tone and impact.
Schindler's List is largely black and white, with controlled exceptions that are a different technique. Grammar of value, not a poster.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Desaturation or Sepia . The tell is leftover blue in shadows, or a brown wash calling itself black and white.
Fix: zero chroma, a real grey scale, texture carrying the image.

faq.q: What is monochrome in film?
faq.a: It is an image with no hue: black and white or another single-scale treatment where value, texture, and shape replace color. Chromatic information is removed or never recorded.

faq.q: Monochrome vs Bleach Bypass
faq.a: Bleach bypass crushes color and adds silver density but usually leaves some hue. Monochrome has no chroma. If you can still name a leftover green or brown as a color in the world, you are not fully mono.

faq.q: When should I use monochrome?
faq.a: Use it when the picture should be a drawing of light and shape. Skip it when leftover color, a brown memory, or a complementary split is the sentence.

faq.q: How do I prompt monochrome for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Monochrome treatment of [Subject], silver highlights, deep blacks, no chroma, shape and light only. Forbid sepia, teal, and residual color accents unless you want a different technique.

title: Moonlight Gel
narrative: A single cool key as the moon, silver edges, ground barely held. Fire, a cabin window, or a lantern can oppose it as a warm hearth.
The audience should feel a source in the sky even when the moon disc is out of frame. It is the wrong tool when you are faking night with underexposed noon ( Day for Night ).

It is the wrong tool when the whole file is merely cooled in the timeline ( Cool Blue ) with no sculpted key. Strongly colored, unmotivated gels (academy reds and greens in Suspiria , nightmare color in Mandy ) are cousins in expressive gel work; if the beat is psychological color rather than a moon, say so, and do not call every gelled nightmare moonlight.
how: Hang a large cool source high, gel toward cyan, steel blue, or pale green, and underexpose the fill so night remains night. Edge the figure with that key; keep faces just inside readability.
A warm practical can sit in the frame as opposition. Control spill so the moon stays one direction.
Prompt: Moonlight gel on [Subject], cyan-green night, a single cool key as the moon, deep underexposure, silver edges.
when: Use it for night that is still sculpted: a forest approach, a snow field, a cabin under a false moon. Do not use it as a blue LUT on day, and do not flatten night into even cool fill.
vs: Cool Blue is a grade. Day for Night is daylight sold as night.
Blue Hour is real dusk. Tungsten Balance will make a cool gel even colder if the camera is set to 3200K.
Hyper-Saturation plus gels becomes expressive color ( Suspiria , Mandy ), which is related gel language but not a moon key.
examples_film: The Revenant uses cool night against fire so moon and hearth compete. The Witch sculpts dark-forest night as a directional cool.
Suspiria and Mandy show how far gel color can leave natural moon; use them as grammar for expressive gels, not as default moonlight. Borrow direction and underexposure.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Cool Blue fill or Day for Night sun. The tell is no key direction, or hard noon shadows tinted blue.
Fix: one high cool source, silver rims, packed night, maybe one warm opposing practical.

faq.q: What is moonlight gel in film?
faq.a: It is a cool gelled key used as moonlight: cyan, steel, or pale green from above, with night still underexposed and sculpted. It is lighting, not only a grade.

faq.q: Moonlight Gel vs Cool Blue
faq.a: Cool blue can be a global grade with no clear source. Moonlight gel is a directional key that stands in for the moon. If there is no silver edge and no dark fill, you probably only cooled the file.

faq.q: When should I use moonlight gel?
faq.a: Use it when night must be sculpted by a moon-like key. Skip it for day-for-night terrain tricks and for even cool fills with no direction.

faq.q: How do I prompt moonlight gel for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Moonlight gel on [Subject], cyan-green night, a single cool key as the moon, deep underexposure, silver edges. Forbid sunny day-for-night cues and even blue fill.

title: Natural Grade
narrative: Style would be a lie. A holiday video that is actually grief, a village in true sun, a fluorescent shop that should stay ugly: the audience is asked to believe the place, not a lookbook.

Fidelity is the point, which is harder than a LUT because every mistake shows as fakery. It is the wrong tool when color must carry a version of the story ( Palette , Color Shift ) or when the world is merciless silver ( Bleach Bypass ).

Filmic Faded can still be fairly natural in hue while lifting the toe; natural-grade is about hue honesty first. Available Light is how you captured it; you can still ruin that capture with a stylized grade.
how: Balance to a plausible white for the location and time of day. Hold skin in a real range (blood, melanin, no teal faces, no plastic orange).
Restrain saturation; do not invent complementary walls. Contrast should match the light you shot, not a trailer.
Prompt: Natural grade on [Subject], faithful skin, restrained saturation, no stylized split, the location's real color science.
when: Use it when style would be a lie: a documentary-adjacent drama, a sunlit memory that must stay ordinary. Do not use it if the beat is a designed palette, a fever, or a complementary poster.
vs: Available Light is the capture sources. Filmic Faded is a print curve that may still be honest in hue.
Teal and Orange and Split Toning editorialize the wheel. Warm Amber and Cool Blue are overall biases.
Natural-grade refuses those biases except what the location already had.
examples_film: Aftersun lets holiday light stay plausible so the grief is not costumed in a look. Timbuktu holds desert and village color as themselves.
Grammar of restraint, not a still to match.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a mild Teal and Orange or a Filmic Faded LUT that still splits hues. The tell is cyan shadows under 'natural', or plastic skin.
Fix: faithful skin, location-true walls and sky, no complementary law, restrained chroma.

faq.q: What is a natural grade in film?
faq.a: It is a color finish that keeps skin faithful and saturation restrained, so the location's real hues remain in charge. The grade refuses a stylized split or a fever.

faq.q: Natural Grade vs Filmic Faded
faq.a: Filmic faded is about the print curve: lifted blacks, rolled highlights. A natural grade is about hue honesty. They can combine, but a faded print can still be teal-orange, which is no longer natural.

faq.q: When should I use a natural grade?
faq.a: Use it when a stylized look would be a lie. Skip it when palette, fever, silver, or a complementary split is the sentence.

faq.q: How do I prompt a natural grade for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Natural grade on [Subject], faithful skin, restrained saturation, no stylized split, the location's real color science. Name place and time. Forbid teal-orange and hyper-saturation.

title: Overexposed
narrative: Blow the whites as a choice. A window becomes heaven or fluorescent hell.
Faces can go toward erasure. The image says there is more light than the medium will hold: revelation, amnesia, a club, a death, a childhood sun that cannot be looked at.

It is the wrong tool when the scene is simply bright and even with detail in the shirts ( High-Key Lighting ). It is the wrong tool for a white flash as an edit event ( Light Flash ) if the shot itself is normally exposed.
Do not underexpose and crush, then call it the opposite. Clipping is directional: you are throwing away the top, not the bottom.
how: Expose until the shoulder clips or the highlights bloom beyond recovery. Decide what must survive (eyes, a silhouette) and let the rest go.

A blooming lens and Halation can soften the burn; a digital clip is harder-edged unless you diffuse. Prompt: Overexposed [Subject], values clipping toward heaven or fluorescent hell, information burned on purpose.
when: Use it when blowing the whites is the sentence: a door onto blinding sun, a memory that erases, a club strobe that stays. Do not use it as a synonym for high-key beauty, and do not clip by accident and keep the take.
vs: High-Key Lighting is low-contrast bright lighting that usually still holds detail. Light Flash is a transient white event, often an edit.
Filmic Faded rolls highlights instead of clipping them. Halation blooms bright points without necessarily destroying the whole shoulder.
examples_film: The Tree of Life lets sun and windows blow so childhood light exceeds the medium. Enter the Void uses overbright interiors and flashes as sensory overload.
Grammar of burned information, not a copied still of a child.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is High-Key Lighting (bright, detailed, low contrast) or a Light Flash cut. The tell is a bright image with texture in the shirts, or a single frame of white in an otherwise normal shot.
Fix: clipped or blooming highlights, lost highlight information, the burn as the point.

faq.q: What is overexposed in film?
faq.a: It is an image whose highlights are allowed to clip or bloom so information at the top of the scale is burned on purpose. Brightness plus lost detail is the fact.

faq.q: Overexposed vs High-Key Lighting
faq.a: High-key lighting is bright and low in contrast, but it can still hold detail in whites. Overexposure throws highlight information away. A white shirt with buttons still visible is not overexposed; it is just bright.

faq.q: When should I use overexposed?
faq.a: Use it when losing the top of the scale is the meaning: blinding sun, erasure, overload. Skip it when you wanted a bright, detailed, high-key scene.

faq.q: How do I prompt overexposed for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Overexposed [Subject], values clipping toward heaven or fluorescent hell, information burned on purpose. Say what still survives. Forbid detailed high-key whites.

title: Palette
narrative: Design as law. A yellow desert chapter, a red-cloth lie, a mint hotel: the audience learns the rule and then feels the break.
Traffic can tint strands so you know which plot you are in. A hotel can live in pinks and purples until a new room breaks the set.
It is the wrong tool when the location must keep its un-designed color science ( Natural Grade ). It is the wrong tool if the only restriction is no chroma ( Monochrome ).
A Split Toning paints the curve; a palette paints the world, including walls and clothes. Palette changes should distinguish meaningful states, not create arbitrary variety.
how: Define a palette rule for each strand across set design, costume, lighting, and grading. Keep the rule stable enough to be learned before breaking it deliberately.
Remove extra hues from frame (a stray neon, a blue plastic bag). Prompt: Restricted palette on [Subject], a few chosen hues doing all the work, design as law.
when: Use it when too many colors would be noise, or when strands of a story must be recognizable by hue. Do not use it as random look-variety, and do not confuse it with a grade-only split on a messy set.
vs: Monochrome is one scale, no hue. Split Toning is highlight versus shadow in the grade.
Color Shift is a change you watch. Hyper-Saturation can live inside a palette ( Hero ) but saturation is not the restriction.
Palette is the designed set of allowed hues.
examples_film: Hero organizes successive versions of events around changing dominant colors. The Grand Budapest Hotel runs hotel spaces as a learned set of pastels and purples.
Traffic uses distinct visual color treatments for different story strands. Grammar of rules, not a still of a desert army.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Split Toning on an uncontrolled set, or a Natural Grade with a LUT. The tell is extra hues leaking from wardrobe and extras, or a grade fighting the furniture.
Fix: control walls, clothes, and lights first, then grade inside that law.

faq.q: What is a palette in film?
faq.a: It is a restricted set of hues used as a rule for a place, a timeline, or a story strand. Set, costume, light, and grade all obey the same few colors.

faq.q: Palette vs Split Toning
faq.a: Split toning colors highlights and shadows in the grade. A palette is designed into the world: walls, clothes, props, and lights. You can split-tone a messy full-spectrum set. A palette would not allow that mess.

faq.q: When should I use a palette?
faq.a: Use it when a few hues should do all the work, or when strands must be recognized by color. Skip it when the real location must remain undesigned.

faq.q: How do I prompt a palette for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Restricted palette on [Subject], a few chosen hues doing all the work, design as law. List the hues. Forbid extra colors in wardrobe and set.

title: Sepia
narrative: A story that already happened often arrives in this brown. Photographs, memory inserts, and period chapters use it because the audience has been trained by albumen and toned prints.
Faded whites, tobacco mids, no true cyan sky. It is the wrong tool when the present should still have a full palette that happens to be warm.
That is Warm Amber or a Filmic Faded print with hues intact. It is also the wrong tool for true Monochrome silver.
If the whole movie is a dusty yellow-brown but still has distinct reds and greens, you are in a restricted Palette or a period DI, not sepia toning.
how: Start from a monochrome or low-chroma image and tone highlights toward paper-gold, mids toward brown, shadows toward umber. Keep cyan and clean white out.
Grain can sit in the mids as in a print. Do not overlay a brown sticker on a saturated modern grade and call it sepia.
Prompt: Sepia tonality on [Subject], brown-gold memory, faded whites, the past as a color, not a filter sticker.
when: Use it for a chapter that already happened: a memory, a found photograph, a prologue. Do not use it as a synonym for any warm movie, and do not leave full modern chroma under the brown.
vs: Monochrome is neutral silver. Warm Amber keeps full color in a honey world.
Filmic Faded lifts blacks and rolls highlights while usually retaining hues. Vintage is a broader period chemistry look that may include sepia but also dye fade and Halation .
examples_film: The Godfather Part II uses warmer, aged memory color for earlier time. O Brother, Where Art Thou?
is a digital period finish in dusty yellow-brown, a cousin often cited when people say sepia. Treat those as grammar for past-as-tone, not as frames to copy.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Warm Amber (full hue, honey mids) or a Instagram brown on a color image. The tell is green trees and blue jeans still speaking as themselves under a wash.
Fix: brown-gold scale, faded whites, almost no leftover modern hue.

faq.q: What is sepia in film?
faq.a: It is a toning of the grey scale into brown-gold, like a chemical print. The past reads as a color. It is not simply a warm grade on a modern palette.

faq.q: Sepia vs Warm Amber
faq.a: Warm amber keeps reds, skin, and lamps as full color in a honey world. Sepia replaces the grey scale with brown-gold and drops modern chroma. One is a grade of a color image. The other is a toned print.

faq.q: When should I use sepia?
faq.a: Use it when a story already happened and should look like a toned photograph or memory chapter. Skip it for present-tense warm interiors.

faq.q: How do I prompt sepia for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Sepia tonality on [Subject], brown-gold memory, faded whites, the past as a color, not a filter sticker. Forbid cyan, saturated primaries, and a full-color amber grade.

title: Split Toning
narrative: Shadows and lights belong to different gods. Gold over teal, magenta over green, steel over amber: the split is a law for the whole image, not a pair of gels in the room.
Drive 's night can feel like candy highlights over cool dark. A future city can put warm sun on one side of the curve and cyan smog on the other.
It is the wrong tool when the split should come from real lamps (a 3200K room and a cold window). That is Tungsten Balance or mixed Practical Lighting , including Neon Practicals .
It is the wrong tool if you only wanted overall steel or overall honey. And it is not bleach-bypass, which is density, not a two-hue curve.
how: In the grade, map the toe to hue A and the shoulder to hue B, with a crossover in the mids you actually like on skin. Keep the pair limited; more hues are not a stronger split.
Test faces at the crossover. Prompt: Split-toned grade on [Subject], highlights one hue, shadows another, for example gold over teal, a two-color world.
when: Use it when highlights and shadows should belong to different hues as a law: a night drive, a future city. Do not use it as a substitute for mixed practicals, and do not assume the pair must be teal and orange.
vs: Teal and Orange is a specific complementary split that also isolates skin. Split-tone is the general method and can be gold/teal, magenta/green, or something else.
Neon Practicals is colored light in the room. Cross Process skews primaries chemically rather than splitting the curve cleanly.
Palette restricts production design hues; split-tone paints the tone curve.
examples_film: Drive often lets night highlights and shadows sit in different hue families. Blade Runner 2049 grades future light so sun, smog, and interior color occupy different parts of the curve.
Grammar of two-hue curves, not a still of a car.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Teal and Orange used as the only imaginable split, or mixed lamps called split tone. The tell is peach skin plus cyan streets with no other pair allowed, or colored neon in the set with a neutral grade.
Fix: declare highlight hue and shadow hue, apply them on the curve, keep the law consistent.

faq.q: What is split toning in film?
faq.a: It is a grade that gives highlights one hue and shadows another. The tone curve becomes a two-color world. The pair can be any two hues, not only teal and orange.

faq.q: Split Toning vs Teal and Orange
faq.a: Teal-orange is one complementary split, usually with protected skin. Split toning is the general tool. Gold over teal, magenta over green, or steel over amber are also split tones.

faq.q: When should I use split toning?
faq.a: Use it when shadows and highlights should obey different hues as a law. Skip it when mixed practicals already tell the color story, or when you wanted a single overall wash.

faq.q: How do I prompt split toning for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Split-toned grade on [Subject], highlights one hue, shadows another, a two-color world. Name both hues. Forbid assuming teal-orange, and forbid calling set neon a split-tone grade.

title: Teal and Orange
narrative: Skin stays peach or tan. Asphalt, night air, and foliage slide toward teal.
Explosions, practicals, and desert sand sit on the orange side. The split is why contemporary studio action reads as punchy: complementary colors vibrate, and the audience still finds a face.
It is the wrong tool when the world should be drained, metallic, and merciless. That is Bleach Bypass , which crushes chroma and raises contrast instead of parking hues on a complementary axis.

It is also the wrong tool if you wanted an overall honey interior ( Warm Amber ) or a steel institution ( Cool Blue ). Taste is the limiter; the split becomes a cliche when every exterior night is the same teal wall.
how: Grade shadows and non-skin midtones toward cyan-teal. Isolate skin so it remains warm; push highlights and practicals toward amber or orange if the scene supports it.
Do not paint half a face teal and half orange unless two sources actually do that. Contrast can be healthy, but this is hue geometry, not silver.
Prompt: Teal-and-orange grade on [Subject], skin staying warm, shadows and skies pushed cyan, complementary split.
when: Use it when you want contemporary studio punch: a night street with warm skin against cyan air. Do not use it on a war or crime world that should feel silver and exhausted, and do not teal every shadow by default.
vs: Bleach Bypass desaturates and densifies; it does not park skin on orange against teal air. Split Toning is the general tool (any highlight hue versus any shadow hue).
Teal-orange is one popular complementary instance, usually with skin isolation. Warm Amber is an overall warm world.
Blockbuster Gloss is a broader finish that often includes this split.
examples_film: Transformers-era Hollywood made the complementary split a default for studio action. Mad Max: Fury Road runs a harsher cousin: fire and chrome-orange against cyan-teal desert air.
Use the hue geometry, not a copied still of a truck.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Bleach Bypass (drained, contrasty, metallic) or a full Cool Blue wash that turns faces cyan. The tell is grey-green skin, or no orange left in highlights.
Fix: warm skin, cyan shadows and skies, complementary split, faces readable.

faq.q: What is teal and orange in film?
faq.a: It is a color grade that parks shadows and skies toward teal or cyan while keeping skin and warm sources orange. Faces stay human; the world splits on a complementary axis.

faq.q: Teal and Orange vs Bleach Bypass
faq.a: Teal-orange is a hue split with protected warm skin. Bleach bypass retains silver, raises contrast, and drains color into a metallic, grainy image. One is complementary grading. The other is density and desaturation.

faq.q: When should I use teal and orange?
faq.a: Use it for contemporary studio punch when warm skin should sit against cool air. Skip it for merciless silver worlds, overall amber homes, and any grade that would turn faces teal.

faq.q: How do I prompt teal and orange for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Teal-and-orange grade on [Subject], skin staying warm, shadows and skies pushed cyan, complementary split. Forbid bleach-bypass grit and a full blue wash.

title: Tungsten Balance
narrative: The room is warm; the world is not. A hotel corridor, a Christmas party, a snowed-in hotel: 3200K lamps own the interior, and the windows go cold.
Mixed sources tell inside versus out without a caption. Safety and exposure can split across a pane of glass.
It is the wrong tool when the whole image should be honey with no cold leftover. That is Warm Amber as a grade.

It is the wrong tool if you paint opposite halves of a face teal and orange without sources to justify it. Do not treat this as a LUT named mixed lighting; it is a white-balance relationship among real lamps.
how: Set white balance near 3200K, or use tungsten stock. Let 5600K windows, moonlight, or cool LEDs go blue.
Keep 3200K practicals as the interior key ( Practical Lighting ). Gels exist to convert sources toward or away from that balance.
Colored light should hit nearby surfaces consistently. Prompt: Tungsten-balanced interior on [Subject], 3200K warmth, windows going cold blue, mixed sources telling inside versus out.
when: Use it when the room is warm and the world is not: a night interior with cold windows, a party against snow. Do not use it to fake a complementary grade without sources, and do not neutralize every lamp to the same white.
vs: Warm Amber is an overall honey grade, not necessarily mixed. Cool Blue chills the whole frame.
Practical Lighting supplies the lamps this balance photographs. Moonlight Gel is a cool key you hang, which will go even colder if the camera is tungsten-balanced.
Split Toning paints highlights and shadows in grade; this is source color at capture.
examples_film: The Shining lets warm interior sources contrast with cold blue window light. Eyes Wide Shut keeps warm practicals and cool night illumination in the same rooms.
Heat and Her also live in mixed-temperature interiors. Grammar of 3200K versus daylight, not a copied wallpaper.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Warm Amber (no cold leftover) or Teal and Orange painted on a face. The tell is a uniformly honey room, or a split face with no window or lamp to cause it.
Fix: 3200K balance, visible warm practicals, daylight or night windows going blue, consistent spill.

faq.q: What is tungsten balance in film?
faq.a: It is white balance (or stock) set for about 3200K. Tungsten lamps look near-white or gently warm, and cooler sources such as daylight windows go blue. Mixed color is kept as information.

faq.q: Tungsten Balance vs Warm Amber
faq.a: Warm amber is a grade that honeys the whole image. Tungsten balance is a capture setting that makes 3200K sources normal and colder sources blue. You can have mixed interiors that are not an overall amber look.

faq.q: When should I use tungsten balance?
faq.a: Use it when inside should be warm and outside cold, or when practicals must stay true while windows go blue. Skip it if every source should match one white.

faq.q: How do I prompt tungsten balance for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Tungsten-balanced interior on [Subject], 3200K warmth, windows going cold blue, mixed sources telling inside versus out. Demand real lamps. Forbid an unmotivated two-tone face.

title: Vintage
narrative: It already happened. Dyes have wandered.
Whites are not video-white. The past is chemistry, not a sticker of scratches.

A 1970s still, a memory sitcom, a period film that wants the stock to confess its age: the treatment says archive even when the camera is new. It is the wrong tool when the only thing you wanted was Cooke swirl on a contemporary story ( Vintage Cine Glass ).
It is the wrong tool when you only wanted toe and shoulder of a print ( Filmic Faded ) with modern dyes intact. Sepia is one brown-gold path through the past; vintage can stay in faded color.
Do not add random specks and call it time.
how: Fade dyes (cyan often goes first in some stocks, or reds go brick), add gentle Halation on practicals, keep contrast modest, and optionally add period-accurate Film Grain . Separate dirt and weave: they are extra claims.
Prompt: Vintage treatment of [Subject], faded dyes, halation, the past as chemistry, not a sticker.
when: Use it when the image should already have happened as an artifact of time. Do not use it as a substitute for vintage glass on a present-tense scene, and do not reduce it to a scratch overlay.
vs: Vintage Cine Glass is the taking lens. Filmic Faded is print curve.
Sepia is brown-gold tone. Halation is bloom on highlights, one ingredient.
Vintage is the combined period chemistry claim.
examples_film: The Master can sit in period-adjacent chemistry as well as character glass; the vintage claim is the whole file looking of an age. Memory-television language (The Wonder Years and similar) treats the past as a softer, drifted color world.
Grammar of faded dyes, not a still to copy.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Vintage Cine Glass (glass only) or a dirty overlay on a modern grade. The tell is sharp modern contrast with specks, or swirl bokeh with contemporary dyes.
Fix: drifted dyes, modest contrast, halation on lamps, time as chemistry.

faq.q: What is vintage in film?
faq.a: It is a period chemistry look: faded dyes, possible halation, and contrast that sits like an aged print or stock. The past is in the file, not only in the costumes.

faq.q: Vintage vs Vintage Cine Glass
faq.a: Vintage cine is the lens: coatings and aberrations. Vintage as a grade or treatment is dye fade and period color chemistry. You can shoot old glass in a modern grade, or modern glass with a vintage treatment.

faq.q: When should I use vintage?
faq.a: Use it when the image should read as already past, as chemistry. Skip it if you only needed old glass, a print curve, or a brown tone.

faq.q: How do I prompt vintage for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Vintage treatment of [Subject], faded dyes, halation, the past as chemistry, not a sticker. Forbid scratch-only overlays and clinical modern contrast.

title: Warm Amber
narrative: Interiors go honey. Skin picks up lamp color.
Windows, if they stay, can go relatively cooler, but the room itself is an invitation. Memory dinners, fairy-tale hotels, and domestic hearths live here because the grade says stay.
It is the wrong tool for a past that should look like a toned print. That is Sepia , brown-gold with chroma mostly gone.
